aria: Animated recap of the Spurs' 124 to 119 comeback win at Chicago: Victor Wembanyama's step-back 3-pointer with 8:19 left, quarter-by-quarter scoring from 22 down, his 32 points, 9 rebounds and 5 blocks, the top scorers, how the Spurs won, and Friday's home game with Golden State.
notes: Box score from the San Antonio Spurs' 124–119 road win over the Chicago Bulls on Nov 11, 2026, from the CBS Sports box score (which carries the play-by-play), checked against the FOX Sports box score, with game details from the AP (Luke DeCock, via KSL), AFP (via Yahoo Sports), the San Antonio Express-News (Jeff McDonald, via Yahoo Sports), Pounding The Rock (via Yahoo Sports) and VAVEL. All 124 San Antonio points and all 119 Chicago points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals (70–56 Chicago at the half; 90–89 San Antonio after three). Bench points (34–59) are worked out from the box score's starters. Records and the Spurs' standing are from the site's standings.

Biggest leads: Chicago's 22, at 64–42 with 5:03 left in the second quarter (Express-News; the AP calls it the Bulls' biggest lead of the season), and San Antonio's 15, at 120–105 with 2:04 left (CBS play-by-play). The Spurs opened the third quarter on an 18–3 run and took the lead at 74–73 (AP, CBS play-by-play), then an 11–2 run early in the fourth took control (AP). It was San Antonio's 10th straight win, finishing a 4–0 road trip (AP), and the Spurs' biggest comeback of the season (Express-News). Wembanyama scored 40 at Phoenix two days earlier (AP). Chicago's Jalen Smith tied his career high with 23 (AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Victor Wembanyama's step-back 3-pointer off Stephon Castle's pass with 8:19 left, which made it 107–94 (CBS play-by-play; VAVEL says the bucket gave him 32 points). The reel draws it as the template's pull-up from deep, not the step-back itself. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the San Antonio Spurs or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Wembanyama’s listed 7-foot-4 and 235 pounds (Basketball-Reference, Wikipedia), with arms scaled to his reported 8-foot wingspan (Wikipedia), in the Spurs' road kit with No. 1 (Wikipedia) and his approved look. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
